title: Marriage as contract
hookLine: consent of both, a gift to the bride, witnesses, a public celebration

lines: A ROOM, A TABLE, A SHEET OF PAPER.
cards: A living room, packed. Aunts on the sofa, kids on the stairs, someone's phone held up to film. On the coffee table, a sheet of paper.
A man asks a question, and a young man answers it out loud: I accept. Somewhere in the room, or just before, the bride has said her yes too. Two people lean in to sign as witnesses.
There's a line on the paper for a gift to the bride. Then someone says mubarak, and the room breaks into noise. No vows invented on the spot.
A question, an answer, a signature, a cheer. Today's word: nikah.

teach.b: Nikah is the Arabic word for marriage, and in Islamic law a nikah is a contract. Its heart is an offer and an acceptance, spoken out loud, in one sitting. One side offers; the other says I accept.
That's the knot. Next, the consent of both.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ says a woman is not to be married until her permission is sought. And Bukhari keeps the story of Khansa bint Khidam, whose father married her to a man she didn't want.
She went to the Prophet, and he annulled the marriage. Her yes was not decoration. Then the other parts.
A gift to the bride, the mahr, which is tomorrow. Witnesses, so the marriage isn't a secret. A public celebration, so the whole neighborhood knows.
Here the schools differ on details.
The Hanafi school allows a grown woman to conclude her own marriage contract; the Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali schools require a guardian, a wali, to conclude it for her, with her consent.
They also differ on how the witnessing and the announcing have to be done. Last, why a contract isn't cold. The Qur'an calls the marriage bond a firm, weighty covenant.

teach.h: A CONTRACT FOR LOVE AND MERCY.
teach.b: And in surah thirty it describes marriage this way, in Pickthall's translation: "He created for you helpmeets from yourselves that ye might find rest in them, and He ordained between you love and mercy."

teach.h: HE ORDAINED BETWEEN YOU LOVE AND MERCY.
teach.b: The paper sets out rights, and the verse sets out what the paper is for: rest, love, mercy. A contract, yes. A contract of mercy.

how: A Muslim marriage is concluded by an offer and acceptance before witnesses, sometimes led by an imam at a mosque or at home, with the bride's consent, an agreed gift to the bride, and a celebration afterward.

games.why: in Bukhari, she went to the Prophet, and he annulled the marriage. her yes was required.

practice: With each breath, set one part down on the coffee table from the hook: her yes and his, the offer and the acceptance, the gift, the witnesses, the celebration.
Then hold a marriage you know, or one you hope for, with two words from the verse: love and mercy. If you pray, you can remember that couple in your own words.

wordCard.voice: Nikah. Marriage in Islam: a contract of offer and acceptance, with the consent of both, a gift to the bride, witnesses, and a public celebration. Today's word.
